items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: It was just the two of us, Bobbie Brown and Jimmy Crawford. So I accepted the gig... she gave me $19.00 for the gig.

ctx.x: And we stayed right on his tail. And so we finally caught him, and so he said, well, here, man. Here's your money. Naturally, we wanted to jump on the guy, but we was too well bred for that, because he didn't know who you -- you know, what you were running into when you jumped down a man and jump on his back and try to do him in.

Well, we got paid. In the meantime, while in Cleveland still a-starving -- this was in, 'round about 1931 or '32 -- Colored, nice looking woman by the name of Brown, Bobbie Brown, pianist, oh, you know, well, she needed a drummer one night. It was just the two of us, Bobbie Brown and Jimmy Crawford.

So I accepted the gig, naturally. I was hungry. And so she gave me $19.00 for the gig. That was more money than I ever had in my life. Me in turn took that -- took part of it or most of it and bought up a whole bag of hot dogs and threw some peanuts in there also, can't get away from those peanuts, and went back to the Majestic Hotel, woke everybody up in the band and said, hey, fellows, let's eat. Whole bag, a bag two feet tall or something like that.
